title: Customer requirements: minimum hardware, network, and security checklist for private deployments
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document captures the minimum customer-side requirements and a compact pre-deployment checklist for Redwood Private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It is intended for customer cloud/platform engineers, SREs, and security teams to verify readiness before a Redwood Private installation or Dedicated integration. The guidance is intentionally conservative: meeting these minimums ensures we can achieve baseline SLOs (99.5%% availability for control plane APIs, 95th percentile p99 token latency targets depending on model class) and run standard day-2 operations (monitoring, upgrades, rollback).

Scope:
- Applies to: Redwood Private Control Plane (VPC-hosted or customer-managed) and On‑Prem inference clusters (in customer datacenter or private cloud).
- Excludes: downstream application-specific scaling beyond baseline capacity (see capacity planning notes in Appendix).

Owner and escalation:
- Redwood contact: Solutions Engineer (assigned per engagement).
- Customer owner: Platform/SRE primary and secondary contacts (provide on kickoff).

Minimum hardware requirements (baseline node roles and counts):

Note: these minimums assume a small production deployment supporting ~5–10QPS of medium-length generation (seq len ~1024). For larger workloads request sizing guidance from Redwood Solutions.

| Role | Minimum nodes | CPU | RAM | Disk (type) | Network |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Control plane (K8s master/control-plane) | 3 | 4 vCPU | 16 GB | 100 GB (SSD) | 1 Gbps redundant |
| Inference worker (GPU) | 2 | 16 vCPU | 64 GB | 1 TB NVMe | 25 Gbps recommended |
| Inference worker (CPU-only, small loads) | 2 | 12 vCPU | 48 GB | 500 GB NVMe | 10 Gbps |
| Storage / artifact nodes (model registry, artifacts) | 1–2 | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 2 TB SSD or NFS | 1–10 Gbps |
| Logging / metrics collectors | 2 | 8 vCPU | 32 GB | 500 GB SSD | 1 Gbps |

Hardware notes and recommendations:
- GPU supported list (minimum recommended): NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 40GB (preferred: A100 for heavy models). For quantized LLMs on Ampere-class cards A30/A10 acceptable for small-medium models.
- Disk: NVMe preferred for model load latency; spinning disks for cold storage only. Use RAID1/10 or cloud-managed persistent disks with IOPS guarantees.
- CPU flags: ensure host kernel has the latest performance patches and configured with transparent hugepages=never for predictable latency.

Network requirements (VPC and on-prem common checklist):

Mandatory network features:
- Private control plane requires stable IPs or DNS entries for: control-plane-api, model-registry, console, metric-ingest.
- Low-latency fabric between inference workers and artifact storage. Recommended intra-cluster latency <500us; network MTU >= 9000 (jumbo frames) where supported.
- Bandwidth: GPU workers should have >=25Gbps NICs; CPU-only workers >=10Gbps.

Firewall and port rules (customer-managed edge and internal firewalls):
- Required inbound/outbound rules between components (examples):
  - Control Plane API: TCP 8443 (HTTPS) inbound from customer admin CIDR + Redwood ops CIDR (if hybrid).
  - Node-to-node gRPC: TCP 50051–50060 (cluster internal) — open within VPC/subnet only.
  - Metrics/Tracing: TCP 9090 (Prometheus pull) or outbound 4317/4318 (OTLP) to configured collectors.
  - SSH for support: TCP 22 (only via bastion; permit Redwood ephemeral IPs when support is active).

DNS, certificate, and TLS requirements:
- Wildcard or explicit DNS entries for control plane endpoints. DNS TTL <= 300s recommended for failover.
- TLS: mTLS for inter-service traffic is strongly recommended. Control plane and console must present certificates from a customer-managed CA or an allowed public CA.
- Cert rotation plan: provide API for cert refresh (ACME or manual) and document expiry/rotation windows.

Security and compliance checklist:
- Identity and access:
  - RBAC: K8s RBAC enabled for control-plane. Cluster admin accounts limited to platform owners.
  - Service accounts: use bound service accounts and least privilege IAM roles in cloud environments.
- Key management:
  - Customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, or HSM) required for encryption of model material and secrets at rest. Provide KMS access policy at least for encryption/decryption.
- Audit logging and retention:
  - Audit logs must be exported to a customer SIEM or cloud logging with retention policy aligned to compliance requirements (default: 90 days).
- Data residency and separation:
  - For regulated customers, provide VPC/subnet isolation for tenant workloads. Ensure no model artifacts or prompt logs cross configured boundaries without explicit consent.

Pre-deployment checklist (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff and contact list: confirm customer SRE, security contact, and RW lead.
2. Inventory and credentials: provide cloud account IDs, VPC/subnet IDs, bastion access, and KMS ARNs.
3. Network validation: customer runs the basic connectivity tests below and provides results.
4. Hardware verification: confirm GPU types, NIC speeds, and disk IOPS numbers (run fio if needed).
5. Certificate and DNS: provide TLS certs (or CSR process) and DNS delegation/records.
6. Security review: share network diagram and IAM policies for assessment.
7. Scheduling: agree on install window and maintenance/upgrade windows.

Connectivity validation commands (examples to run from a customer bastion host):
- DNS: dig +short control-plane.example.internal
- Port test: nc -vz control-plane.example.internal 8443
- Bandwidth test (between worker nodes): iperf3 -c <peer> -P 8 -t 30
- Disk IOPS sample: fio --name=randread --ioengine=libaio --rw=randread --bs=4k --size=1G --numjobs=4 --runtime=30 --group_reporting

Validation tests (post-install smoke tests):
- API health: curl -k -s https://control-plane.example.internal:8443/healthz should return HTTP 200 and JSON {"status":"ok"}.
- Model pull: request a small model install and verify model registry reports state=ready within configured timeout.
- Inference loop: submit a 64-token generation to a lightweight model and verify latency < baseline (see appendix baseline numbers).
- Metrics visibility: Prometheus target list must include all exporter endpoints; no scrape errors older than 5 minutes.

Acceptance criteria (minimum to sign-off):
- All pre-deployment checklist items validated.
- Smoke tests pass in two consecutive runs spaced 30 minutes apart.
- Security and audit logs successfully delivered to customer logging with expected fields (timestamp, principal, action, resource).
- Backup snapshots for artifact storage completed and verified.

Day-2 operations and upgrade guidance (high level):
- Monitoring and alerting:
  - Critical alerts: control-plane unavailable, model-pull failrate >2%% over 10m, GPU OOM events, persistent scrape errors.
  - Suggested SLOs: control-plane p99 API latency < 500ms; model-pull success rate >= 99%%.
- Routine maintenance:
  - OS and driver patching: schedule during agreed maintenance window, cordon and drain worker nodes before driver/OS upgrades.
  - Model updates: treat model updates as application deploys; run canary to 10%% of serving capacity then ramp.
- Upgrade procedure (short checklist):
  1. Announce window to stakeholders and disable auto-scaling for the window.
  2. Snapshot artifact stores and backup etcd (if K8s control plane managed by customer).
  3. Upgrade control-plane services one at a time with health checks between steps (healthz and readiness probes).
  4. Upgrade inference runtime kernel and drivers on a drained node, validate model load, then uncordon.
  5. Run regression smoke tests and monitor for 30–60 minutes.
  6. Rollback immediately if any critical SLO breaches occur or if >5%% request error rate persists for >15 minutes.

Rollback strategy (guiding rules):
- Fast rollback is allowed for control-plane changes or runtime driver patches if smoke tests fail. Use previously tested image tags or snapshots.
- For model rollout regressions, immediately revert routing to previous model variant and scale up previous variant capacity if necessary.
- Keep at least two prior well-known-good control-plane images and model variants available for rollback.

Operational runbook excerpts (what to provide to oncall):
- Incident: Control plane 503s observed across zones — immediate steps:
  1. Check control-plane pods: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide; detect CrashLoopBackOffs.
  2. Inspect control-plane logs: kubectl -n redwood logs <pod> --since=10m.
  3. Validate etcd/DB connectivity and disk pressure.
  4. Notify Redwood support and attach kubectl output bundles.

Appendix A — Baseline latency and load numbers (example):
- Small model: p95 response < 80ms, p99 < 200ms on CPU-only worker.
- Medium model: p95 < 180ms, p99 < 400ms on single A10 GPU.
- Model pull: median model pull time (artifact load to worker) < 45s for 2GB model from local NVMe.

Appendix B — Example minimal IAM policy (cloud):
- Provide a yaml snippet with permissions required by the control plane (S3:GetObject, S3:PutObject, kms:Decrypt).

Appendix C — Contact matrix and runbook links:
- Redwood SRE runbook: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/redwood-private-sre-runbook (internal)
- Onsite escalation: provide customer-specific phone and pager contacts in the deployment intake form.

Notes and change history:
- 2024-08-12: Initial draft, A. Patel.
- 2024-11-05: Added GPU guidance and MTU recommendations, L. Chen review.
- 2025-02-07: Hardened security checklist and added rollback thresholds after customer pilot, Marisol Rivera.

End of document.
